stem.en: An organism has many cells, clear tissues and a backbone, and it breathes in water early in life. Why is mode of nutrition not enough to place it?

text.en: It makes its own food, so nutrition does not apply to it.

feedback.en: An animal with a backbone depends on others for food. It does not make its own.

text.en: It is heterotrophic, but fungi and many bacteria are heterotrophic too.

feedback.en: Right. Depending on others for food is shared by many groups, so nutrition alone cannot place it.

text.en: Mode of nutrition is a feature of single cells, so it says nothing about a body of many cells.

feedback.en: Plants and animals have many cells, and they differ in their mode of nutrition.

text.en: An organism with a backbone has no fixed mode of nutrition.

feedback.en: It does have one: it depends on others for food. The trouble is that many other groups share it.

explanation.en: Heterotrophic organisms are found in several kingdoms. Features such as tissues and a backbone are needed to place this organism.

hints.en: Which other organisms also depend on others for food?
